root_cause: Thyroid storm from Graves' disease flare (stopped medication)

patient.name: Maya Okafor
patient.background: Biology student, Graves' disease diagnosed last year, exam season stress

findings.result: Enlarged, hot gland with heavy blood flow: diffuse goiter
Thyroid hormone sky-high, TSH near zero: hyperthyroxinemia
Fast chaotic rhythm, 160 bpm: atrial fibrillation
Clear lungs, no infection: normal chest
No bleed or stroke on scan: normal CT
High caffeine level, mildly raised: caffeine intake
Liver enzymes mildly raised: hepatic stress
Urine clean, no bacteria: normal urinalysis

treatments.name: Propranolol, PTU, iodine, steroids
treatments.why: Beta-blocker calms the heart, PTU blocks new hormone, iodine halts release later, steroids block T4-to-T3 conversion.
treatments.attending_line: Look at that, you treated the gland instead of its fan club.

treatments.name: Broad antibiotics + fluid boluses
treatments.why: No infection exists; big fluid loads strain a heart already failing from thyroid overdrive.
treatments.attending_line: Sepsis without bugs. Bold. Her lungs are now a swimming pool.

treatments.name: More aspirin for fever
treatments.why: Aspirin knocks thyroid hormone off its carrier protein, raising free hormone and worsening the storm.
treatments.attending_line: You fed the fire a fresh log and called it a fire blanket.

treatments.name: Sedate for caffeine overdose
treatments.why: Caffeine is a red herring; benzodiazepines blunt breathing while hormone excess keeps driving the heart.
treatments.attending_line: Three energy drinks, yes. Also a goiter the size of a lemon.

post_mortem: Maya ran out of her Graves' medication during exams, and the untreated autoimmune thyroid flared into thyroid storm, made worse by the aspirin she took. The clues were the skipped pills, sweating in a cold room, and a hot, enlarged thyroid. The energy drinks only explained a bit of it.
